content: 1. Elevated plasma levels of quinidine may occur, potentially leading to cardiac conduction disturbances and arrhythmias. Close monitoring is advised when using this medication. 2. Sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effects of ramipril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, but monitoring is advised. 4. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Close monitoring is necessary. 5. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels or effects of rifampin through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Concomitant administration of antacids may reduce the absorption of rifampin. Rifampin should be administered at least one hour before antacids. 7. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 8. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Omeprazole decreases the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is contraindicated due to the risk of treatment failure and resistance development. 10. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of riociguat by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and caution is advised. 11. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of riociguat by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and caution is advised. 12. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of risedronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and doses should be separated by two hours. 13. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and caution is advised. 15. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and caution is advised. 16. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of rosuvastatin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and doses should be separated by two hours. 17. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, but monitoring is advised. 18. Sodium bicarbonate increases salicylate levels at moderate doses but decreases them at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 19. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 20. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Dosing of tetracyclines should be separated from these products. 21. Omeprazole may cause a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during secretin stimulation testing, potentially leading to false-positive results for gastrinoma. Omeprazole treatment should be stopped at least 14 days before testing to allow gastrin levels to return to baseline. 22. Sodium bicarbonate and sodium sulfate/potassium chloride/magnesium sulfate/polyethylene glycol can both decrease serum potassium levels. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 23. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and coadministration is not recommended. If necessary, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir should be taken with food four hours before omeprazole. 24. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of sotalol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and doses should be separated by two hours. 25. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and alternative drugs should be considered. 26. Sparsentan decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Omeprazole decreases the effects of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and alternative drugs should be considered. 28. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 30. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of strontium ranelate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and doses should be separated by two hours. 31. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of sulfasalazine by increasing renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 32. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 33. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by affecting the same enzymes. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and alternative drugs should be considered. 35. Omeprazole increases the toxicity of theophylline due to prolonged use of proton pump inhibitors causing hypochlorhydria. Monitoring for toxicity is recommended. 36. Omeprazole decreases the levels of thyroid desiccated by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and its significance is unknown. 37. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of tiludronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and doses should be separated by two hours. 38. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of timolol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and doses should be separated by two hours. 39. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 40. Omeprazole increases the levels of tofacitinib by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 41. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of trandolapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 42. Omeprazole increases the levels of triazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, but monitoring is advised. 43. Triclabendazole increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 45. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the effects of ursodiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 46. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of vismodegib by altering its solubility due to increased gastric pH. Monitoring is recommended, as the effect on efficacy is unknown. 47. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 48. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of warfarin by inhibiting enzymes involved in its metabolism. INR should be monitored more frequently, and warfarin doses adjusted as needed. 49. Sodium bicarbonate increases salicylate levels at moderate doses but decreases them at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 50. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of zoledronic acid by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms, and doses should be separated by two hours. 51. Long-term use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) may lead to atrophic gastritis, acute interstitial nephritis, and an increased risk of Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD). Therapy should be limited to the lowest effective dose and shortest duration necessary. 52. PPIs have been associated with cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Discontinue use if symptoms occur, and refer the patient to a specialist. Most patients improve within 4–12 weeks after stopping PPIs. 53. Observational studies suggest an increased risk of osteoporosis-related fractures with prolonged or high-dose PPI therapy. Patients at risk should be managed according to established guidelines. 54. Relief of symptoms with PPI therapy does not eliminate the possibility of gastric malignancy. Further evaluation should be considered if symptoms persist.
